prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a top-down egocentric view of a small rectangular dining table (about 0.6–1.2 m below and in front of the standing camera wearer) surrounded by six people spaced roughly 0.4–1.0 m apart around its perimeter. Bright white foreground regions (0.2–0.5 m away) highlight the camera wearer's own hands and chopsticks at the bottom center and the adjacent person in the blue top on the bottom left (frames 2–4), both within immediate arm's reach of the bowls, greens, and central divided hotpot on the table. Mid-grey silhouettes (0.8–1.5 m away) capture the seated person in the white shirt at the bottom right, the standing person in the black shirt with hands on hips on the right, and the three people across the top edge (wearing black, yellow, and white tops at 1.2–2.0 m distance) facing inward toward the table and the camera wearer. Across the 5 frames, the camera wearer's viewpoint pans slightly left in frames 2–3 and back right in frames 4–5 while foreground arms extend upward over the table surface, partially occluding the lower dishes and the seated person at the bottom right. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly separates the elevated foreground hands and raised pot rim from the flat tabletop plane, though it is unreliable on thin chopsticks (which vanish or merge into the background) and flattens facial features and the meat trays into uniform grey blobs.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map labels the central surface as a `dining table` (~0.6–1.2 m away) and identifies the large divided hotpot and several side dishes of vegetables and lotus root as individual `bowl` or `cup` instances within arm's reach (0.4–1.0 m) of both the camera wearer and the surrounding group. It segments up to six `person` instances arranged around the table roughly 0.4–0.8 m from each other: one in a blue tank top at the bottom left (0.3–0.6 m), one seated at the bottom right (0.7–1.0 m), three standing or sitting across the far side in black, yellow, and white tops (1.2–1.8 m) facing toward the table and camera wearer, and one standing on the far right (0.9–1.3 m) whose upper body rotates into fuller view by frames 4–5. As the camera pans left and then right across the 5 frames, foreground arms and hands reach from the bottom edge across the lower tabletop, partially occluding the `dining table` mask and the seated person at the bottom right while people at the edges are partly cropped out of the frame. This map delineates distinct person and dish boundaries even in dark, cluttered areas where dark clothing blends into the floor in RGB, but it is unreliable across time—fragmenting the table mask around the raw meat trays, missing the knife and chopsticks entirely, and misclassifying a red armchair strap as a `bottle` in frame 1 and a small condiment container as a `cell phone` in frame 4.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is mostly blank black space that isolates only a few 2D skeletal keypoints (yellow) and hand landmarks (magenta) without rendering the scene layout or tabletop objects. In frame 1, it detects the upper-body torso, head, and arms of the seated person at the bottom right (~0.8–1.0 m away, below and right of center, angled toward the table) with magenta hand keypoints clustered near a white bowl within their arm's reach, and in frame 5 it detects the torso, shoulders, elbows, and facial keypoints of the standing person on the right (~1.0–1.2 m away, facing left toward the table and slightly toward the camera wearer). Across frames 2, 3, and 4, full-body skeletons disappear completely, leaving only isolated magenta hand clusters at 0.3–0.7 m distance in the lower-left and bottom-center foreground as the camera wearer's and the blue-shirted neighbor's hands hold and pass wooden chopsticks over the table. While the pose map makes the exact finger articulation of overlapping hands and the shoulder-elbow geometry of the right-side person easier to isolate than in the busy RGB image, it is highly unreliable overall because severe top-down foreshortening and partial framing cause it to miss all three people across the far side of the table (1.2–2.0 m away) and drop body skeletons in the middle frames.
